poi.ruh_masmak.name: Al-Masmak Fortress
poi.ruh_masmak.culture: 18th-century mudbrick citadel; the gate still bears the spearhead from the 1902 battle that reunified Saudi Arabia.
poi.ruh_natmuseum.name: National Museum of Saudi Arabia
poi.ruh_natmuseum.culture: Eight galleries charting the Arabian Peninsula from prehistoric times through the founding of the modern Kingdom.
poi.ruh_diriyah.name: Diriyah At-Turaif UNESCO District
poi.ruh_diriyah.culture: Birthplace of the Saudi state and a UNESCO World Heritage Site; mudbrick palaces and mosques dating to the 15th century.
poi.ruh_kingdom.name: Kingdom Centre Sky Bridge
poi.ruh_bujairi.name: Al-Bujairi Heritage Park
poi.ruh_bujairi.culture: Restored craftsmen's quarter directly across the wadi from At-Turaif; active art studios and traditional coffee houses.
poi.ruh_boulevard.name: Boulevard World Riyadh
poi.ruh_wadi_hanifah.name: Wadi Hanifah Eco Park
poi.ruh_edge.name: Edge of the World (Jebel Fihrayn)
poi.ruh_edge.culture: 300-metre vertical escarpment overlooking the Tuwaiq valley — locals call it the end of the world.
poi.ruh_camel.name: King Abdulaziz Camel Market
poi.ruh_camel.culture: The world's largest camel market; thousands of camels traded daily. Go before 10am.
poi.ruh_murabba.name: Al-Murabba Historical Palace
poi.ruh_murabba.culture: 1930s mudbrick palace of King Abdulaziz, precursor to the modern capital.
poi.ruh_artdistrict.name: Riyadh Art District (Ithra)
poi.ruh_old_market.name: Al-Zal Old Market
poi.ruh_old_market.culture: Traditional bazaar unchanged since the 1940s; gold, spices, and antique silver.
poi.ruh_red_sands.name: Red Sands Desert (Al-Ramah)
poi.ruh_natlib.name: Saudi National Library
poi.jed_balad.name: Al-Balad UNESCO Historic District
poi.jed_balad.culture: 400-year-old coral-stone houses with intricately carved wooden Rawasheen (balconies); UNESCO since 2014.
poi.jed_fountain.name: King Fahd Fountain
poi.jed_mosque.name: Al-Rahmah Floating Mosque
poi.jed_mosque.culture: Built on stilts over the Red Sea; appears to float at high tide. Open to non-Muslim visitors outside prayer times.
poi.jed_corniche.name: Jeddah Corniche Walk
poi.jed_aquarium.name: Fakieh Aquarium
poi.jed_shallal.name: Al-Shallal Theme Park
poi.jed_khalil_museum.name: Abdul Raouf Khalil Museum
poi.jed_khalil_museum.culture: Private collection covering 7,000 years of Arabian history across four floors; exceptional Islamic manuscript gallery.
poi.jed_nasif.name: Nasif Historical House
poi.jed_nasif.culture: 19th-century merchant mansion where King Abdulaziz stayed during his 1925 campaign; still preserves original furniture.
poi.jed_bab_makkah.name: Bab Makkah Old City Gate
poi.jed_obhur.name: Obhur Creek Beach
poi.jed_nawras.name: Al-Nawras Park Jeddah
poi.jed_heritage_village.name: Jeddah Heritage Village
poi.jed_flower_market.name: Al-Balad Flower & Spice Market
poi.jed_flower_market.culture: Frankincense, oud, and saffron traded in the same alley for five centuries.
poi.jed_waterfront.name: Jeddah Waterfront (North Corniche)
poi.ula_hegra.name: Hegra (Mada'in Salih) — Nabataean Tombs
poi.ula_hegra.culture: Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site; 111 rock-cut Nabataean tombs dating to the 1st century CE.
poi.ula_elephant.name: Elephant Rock (Jabal AlFil)
poi.ula_oldtown.name: AlUla Old Town
poi.ula_oldtown.culture: Abandoned 900-year-old mudbrick settlement; 900 homes, 400 shops, and six mosques awaiting rediscovery.
poi.ula_ikmah.name: Jabal Ikmah (Library Mountain)
poi.ula_ikmah.culture: Open-air library of Lihyanite, Dadanitic, and Minaic inscriptions carved into sandstone cliffs — over 500 ancient texts.
poi.ula_dadan.name: Dadan Archaeological Site
poi.ula_dadan.culture: Capital of the Lihyan and Dadanite kingdoms (9th–1st c. BCE); lion-carved tomb facades visible from the valley.
poi.ula_maraya.name: Maraya — Mirror Building
poi.ula_maraya.culture: World record-holder for largest mirror-clad building; 9,740 m² of mirrored facades reflecting the Ashar Valley canyon.
poi.ula_ashar.name: Ashar Valley Canyon Walk
poi.ula_oasis.name: AlUla Oasis Palm Grove Walk
poi.ula_oasis.culture: Ancient falaj irrigation system still watering 2 million date palms; some trees are over 1,000 years old.
poi.ula_harrat.name: Harrat Uwayrid Lava Fields
poi.ula_winterpark.name: Winter Park AlUla
poi.ula_farms.name: AlUla Date Farm Experience
poi.ula_farms.culture: 70+ named date varieties; farmers still harvest by hand using the same climbing technique as their ancestors.
poi.ula_jabal_ahmar.name: Jabal Al-Ahmar (Red Mountain)
poi.ula_visitor_center.name: AlUla Visitor Experience Centre
poi.ula_dedan.name: Dedan Ancient Kingdom Ruins
poi.ula_dedan.culture: Seat of the Lihyan kingdom; towering lion statues once flanked the entrance to the royal tombs.
dish.kabsa_chicken.name: Kabsa (Chicken)
dish.kabsa_chicken.desc: Fragrant saffron-spiced rice with slow-braised chicken, dried fruits, and fried onions — the national dish.
dish.kabsa_lamb.name: Kabsa (Lamb)
dish.kabsa_lamb.desc: Whole lamb joint slow-cooked with aromatic Kabsa spice blend atop long-grain rice.
dish.jareesh.name: Jareesh
dish.jareesh.desc: Cracked wheat slow-cooked to a creamy porridge with lamb, topped with crispy onions and ghee.
dish.saleeg.name: Saleeg
dish.saleeg.desc: White rice simmered in milk broth with chicken; Hejazi comfort food served with tomato sauce.
dish.maraq.name: Maraq Lamb Broth
dish.maraq.desc: Clear spiced lamb broth with herbs — traditionally the first course of a Saudi feast.
dish.machboos_rubyan.name: Machboos Rubyan (Shrimp Rice)
dish.machboos_rubyan.desc: Gulf-style spiced rice with jumbo shrimp, dried limes (loomi), and rose water — beloved on the Red Sea coast.
dish.sayadiya.name: Sayadiya Fish Rice
dish.sayadiya.desc: Levantine-influenced fish rice; caramelised onion gravy soaks into long-grain rice beneath whole grilled fish.
dish.thareed.name: Thareed (Lamb Bread Stew)
dish.thareed.desc: Thin flat bread layered with slow-braised lamb and vegetables; the Prophet ﷺ described it as the best of foods.
dish.harees.name: Harees
dish.harees.desc: Wheat and lamb pounded to a silky paste; simple, ancient, and deeply comforting.
dish.samboosa_lunch.name: Samboosa Platter
dish.samboosa_lunch.desc: Crispy triangular pastries filled with spiced minced meat, herbs, and pine nuts.
dish.mandi_lamb.name: Mandi (Slow-Roasted Lamb)
dish.mandi_lamb.desc: Whole lamb smoked low-and-slow in an underground pit (tandoor); meat falls from the bone.
dish.madfoon.name: Madfoon (Buried Lamb)
dish.madfoon.desc: Seasoned lamb buried in a sand pit with hot coals overnight; smoky, fall-apart perfection.
dish.ouzi.name: Ouzi (Whole Lamb with Rice)
dish.ouzi.desc: A whole roasted lamb on a bed of spiced rice, crowned with pine nuts and almonds.
dish.mathbi_chicken.name: Mathbi Grilled Chicken
dish.mathbi_chicken.desc: Spatchcocked chicken pressed between two hot stones over open fire — a Bedouin camp classic.
dish.mutabbaq.name: Mutabbaq (Filled Pancake)
dish.mutabbaq.desc: Street-food pancake stuffed with egg, minced lamb, onion, and spices — a Jeddah souk staple.
dish.lahm_basal.name: Lahm bil Basal (Lamb & Onion Stew)
dish.lahm_basal.desc: Slow-braised lamb shanks with caramelised onions in a rich tomato stew.
dish.kabsa_dinner.name: Kabsa Dinner Special
dish.kabsa_dinner.desc: Evening-edition kabsa with added dried apricots, almonds, and golden raisins.
dish.fish_mandi.name: Fish Mandi (Jeddah Style)
dish.fish_mandi.desc: Red Sea fish smoked Mandi-style over wood embers with turmeric and Gulf spices.
dish.shish_tawook.name: Shish Tawook Platter
dish.shish_tawook.desc: Yoghurt-marinated chicken cubes charcoal-grilled on skewers; served with garlic sauce and flatbread.
dish.kunafa.name: Kunafa bil Jibneh (Cheese Pastry)
dish.kunafa.desc: Crispy shredded pastry over white cheese soaked in rose-water syrup — the Middle East's favourite dessert.

profile.signout.title: Sign out of Safarly?
profile.signout.body: This deletes your profile, trips, saved dishes and learned phrases from this device. Nothing is stored anywhere else, so this cannot be undone. Your language and theme settings are kept.
